The choice also changes the comparison group. Under the pooled reference period every untreated observation serves as a control. That includes never-treated cohorts, cohorts treated after the end of the sample, and the pre-treatment periods of cohorts not yet treated, apart from any pre-treatment horizons the run asks for. Parallel trends and no anticipation must then hold across all of those periods. Under *esfixedbaseperiod* each treated cohort's pre-treatment periods other than the reference period carry their own indicators, and the reference period only anchors that cohort's own level. Parallel trends is needed only between each treated cohort and those cohorts, from the reference period on. This is the never-treated comparison of Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) and Sun and Abraham (2021). The pooled default instead matches the imputation estimator of Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2023) under the conditions given in chapter 15.
